bib.title: From simple networks to multisource integration (Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, ch. 4)

question: How do you build, integrate, analyse and interpret biomedical knowledge graphs from several structured sources, with LLMs in an auxiliary role?
contributions: Three biomedical case studies (PPI/disease, Hetionet, Clinical Knowledge Graph) with Neo4j import and analysis code
Graph-level (WCC, Louvain) and domain-specific (largest component, density, conductance, DWPC) analysis
LLM prompts that interpret KG analysis results

results.claim: The authors say LLM output must be interpreted by physicians and researchers.

limits: LLM interpretation (Claude.ai Sonnet 4.0) is shown only as a partial sample with no evaluation; the clinical-prompt output is not shown.
Louvain modularity is printed as 0.5464 in Table 4.2 and as around 0.40 in the prose.
Many numbers (disease pathway medians) come from figures 4.7 and 4.8 with the prose giving only a few.
Formulas (PDP, DWPC, density, conductance) are images and absent from the cached text.
Authors state LLMs play complementary but limited roles here; traditional data integration does the construction.
practices: Define node key constraints before importing (Listing 4.1).
Load in batches with MERGE, IN TRANSACTIONS OF 100 ROWS (Listings 4.2-4.5).
Map disease identifiers from different databases to a shared code such as UMLS before merging (4.2, Yang et al.).
Check counts after each import step (Exercises in 4.2.1).
Start graph evaluation with WCC and Louvain, then use domain-specific metrics because generic algorithms treat all nodes alike (4.2.2).
Use DWPC rather than raw path count to avoid well-known hub nodes (4.3).
Use statistical relationships rather than patient records, or deidentified data, for clinical KGs (4.4).
Do not use LLM output without expert interpretation (4.4.1).

terms.definition: a sequence of node and relationship classes that describes potential real paths between a node of the first type and a node of the last type
the number of paths, of a specified metapath, between the defined source and target nodes; each path has a value of 1
the sum of path-degree products for a metapath; each degree is raised to the -w power, w >= 0 the damping exponent
an undirected subgraph of the PPI network specified by the set of proteins associated with the disease
the independence of the disease pathway from the rest of the graph; lower means a tighter-knit community
